mechanism_narrative: The level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuation and increase the attractiveness of equities relative to fixed income.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return correlation with FEDFUNDS level is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a severe economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.5pp and UNRATE increases by > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in instances where FEDFUNDS rises >0.5pp and UNRATE rises >0.2pp in 3 months are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized), a high housing starts index (HOUST) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as strong economic growth increases demand for housing and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in instances where GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 3-month average (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The level of industrial production (INDPRO) is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as higher industrial output signals robust economic growth and stronger corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return correlation with INDPRO level is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in instances where UNRATE > 4.5% are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by > 0.5% and INDPRO decreases by > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in instances where PAYEMS falls >0.5% and INDPRO falls >0.5% in 3 months are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) falls below 95.0, it signals a contraction in manufacturing and services, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in instances where INDPRO < 95.0 are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
